steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
In a medium bowl, stir together the honey, soy sauce, lemon juice and sesame seeds. Dip the pieces of chicken into the sauce to coat, then place in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish.
Bake for about 45 minutes in the preheated oven, until chicken is cooked through and sauce is caramelized.

raw_recipe.headline: Sticky Sesame Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken thighs are coated in a honey lemon sauce with sesame seeds, then left to bake for an effortless meal. An easy way to prepare chicken that is economical too. Both my husband and my children love it!

video.description: This easy and budget-friendly recipe is perfect for a weeknight dinner!
video.name: How to Make Sticky Sesame Chicken

Bake for about 45 minutes in the preheated oven, until chicken is cooked through and sauce is caramelized.

review.reviewBody: good for how easy it was to make, I added ground ginger for some extra taste. Next time I think I will add peanut butter and chili garlic sauce

My family really liked this recipe but I did make some changes. I used half soy sauce and half teryaiki sauce to make up the 1/4c. in the recipe. I also added fresh diced ginger and used orange juice instead of lemon juice. I used this mixture to dip the chicken into and then sprinkled the sesame seeds on top. I then added 1 tbsp. of cornstarch to the mixture and heated it until thick. This was the sauce I spooned over the chicken before putting it into the oven. It was really good served with broccoli and rice.
Recipe is very good! Cubed the chicken, Added some garlic. Served with rice and stir fried green beans, broccoli & red peppers!

I forgot to use the lemon juice, and I used 50/50 of honey and soy. 

It was amazing. I'm saving this one off.

Add a Tbsp. of Thai chili paste to make this more like a General Tsao chicken dish!!

For a quick meal it was pretty good with a couple of tweaks. I decided to fix it on the stove top in a non stick pan. I started with the ingredients as written, heated sauce tasted and then added about 2 Tbs peanutbutter, 1 Tbs sweet chili sauce, would have added fresh Ginger but didn't have any, then added a dash of 5 spice. Once I got the sauce flavorful I added the cut chicken thighs and sautéd until chicken was done and sauce was nice and sticky. Served with grilled asparagus over rice.

The first time I made this, I loved the flavour, but didn't like that the sauce seemed thin. Still, I would give it four stars. To make it even better, though, here's what I do: (1) remove from oven, (2) remove chicken and pour sauce into pan, (3) bring to a boil, (4) mix together 1/4 c cold water and 1 1/2 tbsp flour and whisk into the boiling sauce, (5) cook until thickened and pour over chicken. You may have to adjust the amount of flour, depending on the desired thickness and amount of sauce.

It's more a flavor of soy sauce than honey or sesame. Perhaps it would be tastier if you put some dark sesame oil in the marinade. Don't put the seeds in the liquid. After marinating in the liquid for 10 minutes, roll in the seeds. Make sure each chicken piece is about the same size and depth for even cooking. A big plus is how easy and quickly it is made.

Ridiculously easy to make and very very good. I only had a little bit of honey so I did 1/4 cup honey but added 1/4 cup of maple syrup. I also salted and peppered the chicken before I added the sauce. The result was spectacular. Everyone loved it and I will be making this again. A recipe does not have to be complicated to be good. The only thing I will do next time is flip over the chicken during cooking so it can soak in the flavor on both sides. When done don't dump the juice, use it as a sauce for rice or some other side. Yummy.

I added peanut butter, chili sauce, Sriracha and cubed the chicken and marinated it in the refrigerator for about an hour prior to cooking. I served over basmati rice. Very yummy and flavorful. This one is a keeper!

Needs MORE Spices.... or marinated for 4+ hours.... there are better honey baked chicken recipes for me. Honey Baked Chicken II and Baked Sweet and Sour Chicken Thighs were great, this Sesame recipe was bland.

We liked this but I would have liked it better if the sauce was thick. It never "glazed" for me. Instead, it was very thin. I will make it again but I will cook the sauce first and thicken it with cornstarch before pouring it over the chicken.
I really enjoyed this actually! I agree that the sauce didn’t get “sticky” for me, but it was still tasty! I did add some granulated garlic to it on top before popping in the oven.
WOW love the recipe. Great dinner. Thank you❤
It was not sticky as the sauce did not stick to the chicken.
This is okay. It was fine for a dinner. Kind of plain.
I made this for my Inuit grandmother's birthday and she absolutely loved it! it tastes great and the way it caramelized in the oven makes my mouth water everytime I think about it. Great job, 10/10!
Followed recipe as is, I think my package of chicken was slightly more by 1/4lb though. I would probably reduce sesame seeds by half. There were just too many
Flavor was fantastic Will definitely make again.
An easy recipe with great flavor! Thanks.
Very good, next time I will make enough sauce to serve the chicken over rice.
